Mastering Asyncio in Python 3.12

Written by David Vance

Python's asynchronous programming model has matured significantly over recent major releases, introducing task groups, enhanced exception groups, and zero-cost exception handling.

Task groups provide a structured concurrency paradigm, guaranteeing that child tasks spawned within a scope are cleanly awaited or cancelled before exiting. This eliminates dangling tasks and unhandled coroutine leakages that historically plagued complex async applications.

Furthermore, custom event loops and uvloop integration enable Python asynchronous servers to achieve throughput metrics comparable to native Go and Node.js networking runtimes.
